messages:
maria-cs: FYI OptiCart just reported a serious perf regression after we rolled out INT8 calibration v2 to their dedicated pool. Their p95 latency went from ~120ms to ~220ms. They see lower throughput too. They say FP16 was consistently faster before the change.

deploy-bot: deployment completed: service=opticart-int8-calib-v2, sha=6f4b2a, nodes=3, region=us-west2 :white_check_mark:

maria-cs: Customer repro steps (they shared):
1) POST /v1/generate model=redwood-7b-mix-quant-int8-calib-v2, batch_size=1, seq_in=32 seq_out=64
2) Send 1000 concurrent single-request clients
3) Observe p95 and overall throughput drop vs a FP16 baseline

maria-cs: Attached snippet from their latency log: ````
[2026-03-12 14:02:13] request_id=abc123 model=redwood-7b-mix-quant-int8-calib-v2 hw=a100-40gb latency=218ms p90=180ms p95=219ms
[2026-03-12 14:02:14] request_id=def456 model=redwood-7b-mix-fp16 hw=a100-40gb latency=118ms p90=95ms p95=122ms
````

luca-runtime: Thanks — looping in eng/runtime and ml. Quick Qs: do we know if KV cache was enabled for customer's request? any token prefix reuse? also are requests routed to the quant slow-path kernels (we saw that after some calib changes)?

maria-cs: KV cache is enabled (they are infilling with conversation state). They said they didn't change client batching. Traffic pattern looks identical.

jess-eng: I'm starting a local repro with their model + calibration artifacts. My first guess: the new calibration changed per-channel scales such that requant/dequant boundary kernels trigger for common seq lengths, which forces a non-fused kernel and extra CUDA kernels per token. Profiling coming. :mag:

sam-ml: Adding context — calibration v2 introduced asymmetric per-tensor 8-bit scale adjustment to reduce distillation loss. That can increase the number of int->fp conversions when KV cache uses fused attention kernels that expect consistent quant params. If kernels detect mismatch they fall back to a safe (slower) pathway.

jess-eng: Quick profiler dump from a repro run on a dev node (trimmed): ````
TIMELINE
kernel_launch_count: 3421
int8_fused_attention_fastpath: 96
int8_fallback_attention_generic: 3225
kv_cache_rewrite_overhead_ms: 73
cuda_memcpy_device_to_device_ms: 28
cpu_quant_postprocess_ms: 41
````
jess-eng: Looks like >90% of attention steps went to the fallback kernel. That would explain the 2x p95.

luca-runtime: Any differences in batch sizes or seq length distribution vs. FP16 can also trigger kernel selection changes. Customer claims single-req clients with batch=1, but internal batching (continuous batching) might coalesce differently under INT8 calibration due to changed execution timing.

olivia-se: From comms side — customer wants immediate mitigation. Options: rollback to FP16 for them, pin old calibration profile, or route their requests to a dedicated FP16 pool while we investigate. Preference?

maria-cs: They asked for the fastest path forward — they want either rollback or routing to FP16. They prefer not to lose availability.

jess-eng: Mitigation plan I recommend: 1) temporary traffic split -> 100% FP16 for OptiCart via routing policy (fastest). 2) Parallel: reproduce at scale and identify kernel selection trigger. 3) If we find that calib v2 causes mismatch flags, create a microfix to normalize scales before handing to fused kernels (hot patch).

sam-ml: We should validate whether the calibration artifacts include per-layer quant params in a format the runtime expects. If there is an extra meta field we introduced, runtime might be ignoring fused-compat hints. Quick check: can we dump the calib json?

maria-cs: Pasted sanitized calib manifest from customer: ````
{"model":"redwood-7b-mix","calib_version":"v2","layers":256,"per_channel_scales":true,"meta":{"asymmetric":true}}
````

jess-eng: Bingo — asymmetric flag wasn't present in v1. Runtime's kernel selector currently assumes symmetric scales for fused attention. With asymmetric flags we take the safe path. That's the regression.

luca-runtime: OK here's immediate action items: 
- @olivia-se coordinate routing change to FP16 for OptiCart and send customer comms (CS-approved text below).
- @jess-eng open a runtime PR to add an early-normalization step when asymmetric scales detected (hot-path). Mark P0.
- @sam-ml add test vectors and a small calibration compatibility check to CI.
- @maria-cs confirm rollback vs routing preference with OptiCart and implement once approved.

olivia-se: Draft comms for OptiCart: "We’ve identified that the new INT8 calibration profile triggers a conservative kernel path in our runtime, causing increased latency. We can either route your traffic to FP16 immediately (no downtime) or pin your pool to the previous calibration while we deploy a fix. Which would you prefer? We recommend routing to FP16 for lowest risk." Ready to send after confirmation.

maria-cs: Customer asks to be routed to FP16 for now — they want stable latency while you work on a fix. Please do the split and confirm.

deploy-bot: routing update: service=opticart, previous_route=quant-int8-calib-v2, new_route=fp16-canary-2026-03-12, change_id=route-789 :rocket:

ops-bot: alert: increased CPU usage observed on fp16-canary-2026-03-12 nodes (expected due to FP16 memory/perf profile). Monitor for hot spots.

jess-eng: I'll open the PR now and tag you @luca-runtime. High level: detect asymmetric flag and either convert to symmetric scales (fast) or synthesize a fused-compatible meta field. If that looks risky we'll implement pre-fusion requant normalization in a follow-up.

sam-ml: I'll add unit tests using the OptiCart calibration artifact and synthetic traces to ensure kernel selector picks fused path.

maria-cs: I'll reply to OptiCart: routing to FP16 is live, performance should return to baseline within 2 mins, and engineering is working on a fix. I'll update them after PR lands and we validate.

olivia-se: Sent message to customer (screenshot attached). They replied: "Appreciate the quick action. Please keep us posted." :thumbsup:

jess-eng: PR: https://git.redwood/infer/runtime/pulls/1425 -- title "handle asymmetric calib scales for fused-attention kernel selection". Brief: detect asymmetric flag, normalize scales for fused path. Marked as urgent.

luca-runtime: Thanks team. Postmortem checklist: 1) Add compatibility test for calib metadata in onboarding checklist. 2) Add telemetry metric for "fallback_attention_generic" count exposed on per-model dashboards. 3) Run a limited canary of next calib release and track kernel path selection.

maria-cs: Customer followup scheduled in 1h. Will update thread with closure. :spiral_calendar:

olivia-se: Great work. :clap:

maria-cs: Update: OptiCart confirmed latency returned to baseline under FP16 routing. Engineering validated PR on staging. Customer asked to be notified before we re-enable int8 on their pool.

jess-eng: Merged PR with hotfix to normalize asymmetric calib metadata. Will coordinate a controlled rollback to quant-int8 after canary and perf check.

maria-cs: Thanks everyone — I’ll coordinate the re-enable window with customer. Closing loop once they're back on INT8 and perf is stable. :white_check_mark:
